note: The SessionStart hook injects the seat once at boot; over a long session it decays, and a compaction can drop it. hooks/reinject.py re-emits a compact, deterministic, fail-open subset of the load-bearing rules, wired to UserPromptSubmit and PreCompact. Clean-room: the disler hooks collection is unlicensed and was not used; the pattern (a hook whose stdout becomes injected context) is reimplemented from the official Claude Code hooks docs. Built by a subagent, integrated here.

decisions.question: Re-emit the whole seat each turn, or only a subset?
decisions.commitment: A compact subset — the governance line, decisions->store, the consult command — never the full boot. anchor() is ~401 chars against build_context()'s ~2527, and re-runs neither pytest nor the brain self-test.
decisions.why: The full seat is injected once because it is expensive (a pytest subprocess and a live store round-trip). Paying that on every UserPromptSubmit would tax every prompt to restate rules that have not changed. The decay being repaired is the agent forgetting three rules, not the readiness checks going stale.

decisions.question: Where does the propose-don't-confirm rule come from — read from seat.md, or a constant?
decisions.commitment: A module constant, verified against hooks/seat.md but never supplied by it. Missing seat.md -> a status line that still carries the rule; a seat.md that lost the line verbatim -> a drift flag. Both proven by a test.
decisions.why: CLAUDE.md keeps this exact line in two files and says why: it drifts. An anchor that could only quote a file present on disk would go silent at compaction time — precisely when the file may be out of context and the rule matters most.
